newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM says Q3 96 cargo revenues up 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: KLM says Q3 96 cargo revenues up 4 pct.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said cargo revenues for the third quarter increased by four percent to 470 million guilders.
The airline said cargo traffic and capacity growth was strongest to and from Asia Pacific and Africa, for the third quarter to end-December last year.
However, KLM capacity to and from Latin America, primarily in the cargo market, had been reduced by three percent,it added in a statement.
"The policy of limited capacity growth resulted in a stable load factor and a slight increase in yield during the third quarter compared to the previous year," KLM said.
Overall, for the nine months ending December 31, 1996, traffic and capacity (which includes both passenger and cargo figures)rose by seven percent.

In the cargo market, traffic growth was particularly strong to and from the Middle East and South Asia. This saw an increase of 20 percent, the airline said but did not provide specific cargo figures.
Revenues for the nine month period increased by three percent to 1,297 million guilders.
Yields in December,(including the fuel surcharge) showed an increase of 6.8 percent, it added.

KLM said the trimming of cargo capacity growth positively influenced overall yield per revenue tonne-kilometre and traffic increases would have their full effect in the fourth quarter, stated the carrier.
A new information technology system to optimise capacity utilisation had also been introduced into the Cargo Division, KLM said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44-171-542-7706 Fax +5017
